data.name: Hariram
data.gender_notes: Hariram is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Hariram is a combination of two popular Hindu deity names, Hari and Ram. Hari refers to Lord Vishnu, the preserver of the universe, while Ram signifies Lord Rama, an avatar of Vishnu known for his righteousness and courage. Therefore, Hariram is a name that symbolizes the divine qualities of both these deities. The name Hariram carries the meaning “Hari (God Vishnu) + Ram (God Rama)” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Hariram usually hope their child will grow to embody hari (god vishnu) + ram (god rama) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace the divine qualities of love, courage, and righteousness.
data.etymology: Hariram belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Hari (God Vishnu) + Ram (God Rama).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hariram total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.
